purpose: Predeclare the human oral-glucose endpoint review for P4 without inventing biological tolerances or fitting the synthetic bridge to summary statistics.

primaryCandidate.evidenceInspected: Primary study abstract, live on 2026-09-22; publisher full PDF returned HTTP 403.
primaryCandidate.preparation: Human vastus lateralis biopsy before and 60 minutes after a 75 g oral glucose load

measurements.endpoint: Transporter-mediated uptake into isolated plasma-membrane vesicles

primaryCandidate.primaryObservableProposed: Within-donor log post/basal membrane-GLUT4 abundance at 60 minutes, after an admitted mapping from the model membrane pool to the assay recovery compartment.
notEquivalentTo: Direct count of the rendered GLUT4 markers
admissionBlockers: Full methods and paired donor measurements are not available in the inspected abstract.
Confirm error-bar definition and membrane recovery/normalization; ratio of group means is not mean paired fold change.
Map sarcolemmal and T-tubule contributions and the model percent-pool denominator to the assay.
Pin plasma insulin/glucose exposure and meal formulation; an abstract-level 75 g glucose load is not a mixed-meal input.
Check independence from Sedaghat calibration/source data before naming this a held-out endpoint.

systemicCandidate.protocol: 1 g/kg oral glucose; five-hour isotope, calorimetry and forearm-balance study
systemicCandidate.reason: Oral-load-specific tracer disposal cannot be equated to all glucose crossing the model muscle boundary. Net exchange, oxidation, storage and total versus meal-derived glucose need separate observation mappings.

requiredBeforeFitting: Acquire and version permitted data with checksums and extraction uncertainty.
Freeze assay observation model, basal initialization, exposure, parameter bounds and calibration/held-out split.
Derive and lock the numeric interval from donor, assay and extraction uncertainty before seeing model predictions.
Evaluate predeclared endpoints and retain failures; never borrow numerical conservation tolerances as biological bounds.

engineeringScope: P4 may demonstrate conservative causal back-coupling using synthetic secretion and uptake laws. Passing that test does not satisfy the human-response phase gate.
